notes: Phase A of docs/model-eval-baseline-proposal.md. One role bundle varies per arm, so a
measured difference can be attributed to a bundle rather than to ten simultaneous changes.
Every role is pinned in every arm: a pinned role reports task-override as its policy
source, and automatic repair escalation applies only to unpinned roles.
Cases are replays of completed real tasks. Each has a known delivered implementation to
anchor the rubric against, which an invented case does not.
The baseline matrix is written out explicitly so the reference arm is a frozen record
rather than whatever the shipped defaults happen to be on the day of the run.
Every repositoryPath is a dedicated eval worktree pinned at that case's frozen base,
not the operator's live checkout. Task creation requires HEAD == frozenBaseSha, so the
checkout has to sit still for the whole of a case's arms; doing that in a live checkout
would detach the branch an operator or another agent is working on. A disposable
worktree can be moved between cases freely and is not shared with any other work.

B0-baseline.description: Shipped Codex standard matrix. Reference arm.

A1-build.description: Build bundle on Claude Sonnet 5 xhigh; every other role baseline.

A2-decide.description: Decide bundle on Claude Opus 5 xhigh; every other role baseline.

A3-understand-cheap.description: Understand bundle dropped from xhigh to high; every other role baseline. Tests whether the cheap majority of stages can be cheaper for free.

cases.shape: consequential backend aggregation following an existing pattern
cases.title: Prompt A — shared-remedy fee grouping
cases.description:
Implement shared-remedy fee grouping in eversor-plancheck. Branch off
evesor-plancheck/main (the remote is `evesor-plancheck`, NOT origin).

Problem: when six claims are all closed by one deliverable — one Schedule of
Prices, one responsibility matrix — each claim currently carries its own
PRODUCE_SCHEDULE fee and the tender's remedy subtotal bills it six times. Every
claim must be retained; only the fee is counted once.

FOLLOW THE EXISTING PATTERN, do not invent one. Construction pricing already
solved the equivalent problem: read backend/variation_costs/aggregation.py,
which groups by `change_group_id` (a reviewer-set group) falling back to
`event_key`, counts one amount per event, reports `shared_claims`, and marks a
group `disputed` when members disagree rather than silently picking one.
Mirror that design and its safety property.

Requirements:
- A reviewer attaches claims to a named remedy group with one common
  deliverable and one editable fee. Append-only revisions, consistent with
  backend/remedy_prices' existing revision model.
- The fee counts ONCE per group in every subtotal. Separately-priced extra work
  on a member claim is preserved and still counted.
- No claim is deleted, hidden or merged. A grouped claim still renders.
- Where members disagree, follow aggregation.py: report it, do not pick one.
- Surface the group and the shared count on Review, All Tenders and Command
  Deck, and make the three agree. Read backend/deck/ and backend/tenders/
  measurements.py (`cost_to_close`) — they must not double-count.
- dbmate migration for any new table. Never create tables from Python.

Read AGENTS.md and backend/AGENTS.md first. backend/remedy_prices/models.py's
docstring states the invariants — the table prices the FIX, never what the
variation is worth unfixed. Do not add a confidence, probability or expected
value field.

Verify: python -m pytest, make integration-test (asserts zero skips),
cd frontend && npm run test, make backend-quality, npm run api:types.
`make e2e-native` has a floor of 2 failed (03-tender-parity colspan, broken on
main too) — that is not your regression.

Report before/after remedy subtotals per tender. Do not merge. No detection,
REMEDY, adjudication or model runs. No Azure changes.
acceptanceCriteria: A shared remedy group counts its deliverable fee exactly once in every subtotal.
No claim is deleted, hidden or merged; a grouped claim still renders.
Disagreeing group members are reported as disputed rather than silently resolved.
Review, All Tenders and Command Deck agree on the group and its shared count.
Any new table arrives via a dbmate migration, never from Python.

cases.shape: migration plus read model plus UI
cases.title: Prompt C — persist match candidates and surface ambiguity
cases.description:
In eversor-plancheck, `backend/variation_costs/scenarios.py` `match_claim`
returns a Match carrying `candidates` — every scenario whose asset AND work
terms fired. `construction_pricing_results` has no candidates column, so it is
computed and thrown away at persist time. The UI therefore cannot say WHAT a
claim was ambiguous between. There is no recorded reason for the omission in
db/migrations/20260909002000_construction_pricing.sql; treat it as an oversight.

Branch off evesor-plancheck/main (remote is `evesor-plancheck`, NOT origin).

1. dbmate migration adding a candidates column to construction_pricing_results.
   Never create or alter tables from Python.
2. Persist candidates for every result, not only ambiguous ones.
3. Expose them on the read model and render on Review: an ambiguous claim shows
   "N scenarios fit this claim, needs review" and lists them by title, each
   selectable in one click. Selecting records a user link — that path already
   recomputes via calculate(origin="user") from the catalogue, so it cannot
   carry bad provenance.
4. CRITICAL: an ambiguous claim's amount must NOT enter any subtotal until a
   reviewer picks. Follow the existing `outcome_excluded` pattern in
   backend/variation_costs/service.py — the value exists, the UI explains it,
   and it is withheld from every total. Make the ambiguous state visually loud;
   the exclusion from the subtotal is the load-bearing half.
5. Same treatment for `incompatible` (currently 2 claims). Today it renders
   identically to "we have nothing", but it means "we found something and
   deliberately refused it" — a different conversation. Say which scenario was
   refused and why.

Current counts on the live local DB: 21 matched, 125 no_match, 2 incompatible,
1 ambiguous of 149 claims. Subtotals must not move for the 21.

Read AGENTS.md and backend/AGENTS.md first. Verify with python -m pytest,
make integration-test (zero skips), cd frontend && npm run test,
make backend-quality, npm run api:types. `make e2e-native` has a floor of
2 failed (03-tender-parity colspan, broken on main too).

Do not merge. No detection, REMEDY, adjudication or model runs. No Azure.
acceptanceCriteria: A dbmate migration adds a candidates column to construction_pricing_results.
Candidates are persisted for every result, not only ambiguous ones.
Review shows how many scenarios fit an ambiguous claim and lists them selectably.
Selecting a candidate recomputes through the catalogue with user origin.
